text.p: British security-to-mobile phones group Securicor Group Plc said on Thursday two one-off exceptional items should not disguise the fact its security and distribution divisions performed well in the first half year.
Exceptional items totalling 28.9 million stg in the six months to March 31 "tend to mar the situation," chief executive Roger Wiggs told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Stressing a "solid performance in security and continually good results in distribution," Wiggs said the underlying trading performance of Cellnet had been "excellent" with growth of about 22 percent over the same period last year.

However, the group announced a 10 million stg provision as its share of a total 25 million stg provision Cellnet has made against delays to completion of a new billing and customer centre service operation.
Securicor holds 40 percent in Cellnet, Britain's second biggest mobile telephone firm, with British Telecommunications Plc holding the other 60 percent.

Securicor finance director Christopher Shirtcliffe told Reuters that the project, whose total cost will amount to just over 70 million stg, had like many major computer projects been "a little bit delayed and a little bit overspent".

"The board felt it appropriate to provide a 25 million provision against the cost of those delays....That is a one-off exceptional item which will not reoccur and which directors are certain is adequate to cover the totality of the delays".

The other exceptional item, announced in March, relates to an 18 million stg charge within Securicor Cellular Services Ltd (SCS) resulting from a change in the period of amortisation on deferred dealer commissions from three years to two years.
Wiggs stressed both exceptional items were "one-offs".
The group reported pretax profits before exceptional items and discontinued operations of 56.1 million stg for the six months to March 31, versus 57.7 million previously.

The results were tempered by losses at SCS and development costs at Intek Diversified Corp, the U.S.-based mobile radio network operator, in which it holds a 63 percent stake after the merger between Securicor Radicoms and Intek.
The communications division made an operating loss of 7.9 million stg, which was predominantly due to start-up costs of 4.6 million stg in the first half at Intek, said Wiggs.
Shirtcliffe said the losses at Intek were much as planned, and it expects Intek to reach a break-even position once it has 50,000 subscribers, which should take a couple of years.
SCS, the group's cellular service provider dedicated to the Cellnet network, incurred trading losses of 3.9 million stg in the first half.

Increased competition from Orange Plc and One 2 One -- jointly owned by Cable & Wireless Plc and US West Inc -- along with the costs of migration to the new digital network and the change in customer profile away from business clients, all contributed to squeezing profits, said Shirtcliffe.

While losses are seen continuing at SCS and development costs at Intek will continue to affect results, chairman Sir Neil MacFarlene said in the results statement: "We have confidence in the longer term performance of communications".
The security division saw operating profits up 43 percent at 5.8 million stg in the first half.

Distribution showed a four percent increase to 12.7 million -- although a later Easter this year resulted in the loss of two working days worth some 800,000 stg in pretax profit, which now will benefit the second half.
"The opening two months have started very well in security and distribution," Wiggs added.
